_comment: P2-132 slice (a): the 'Max contracts per account' sizing rule reports currentValue=null while the enforcer reads the live position every sweep, so a rule in breach (11 against a cap of 10, measured on TAKEPROFITPRO524207503) renders identically to one that has never come close -- while three neighbouring rules (Daily loss limit, Max trades per session, Max consecutive losses) all report where you stand. This slice fixes ONLY the per-account contract cap's currentValue by deriving it from the same position data GetAccountSnapshots already gathers. It does NOT touch the aggregate cap (its currentValue is a cross-account sum, a separate computation) and does NOT touch the EvaluatedNotEnforcing state-vocabulary half (b) -- both get their own slices. Reporting-only, shadow-safe: nothing about enforcement changes.

tickets.title: The per-account contract cap reports the live position instead of null
tickets.defect: GuardRuleRegistry's 'Max contracts per account' evaluator returns R(null, c.Config.Sizing.MaxContractsPerAccount, ...) -- a hardcoded null currentValue -- while the enforcer in RiskGuardAddOn reads pos.Quantity every sweep and locks out on 'pos.Quantity > limit'. Measured live on TAKEPROFITPRO524207503: nt_positions showed MNQ Long 11 against a cap of 10, MAX_SIZE_BREACH fired at the second the 11th lot filled, and the rule inventory still reported currentValue:null. This is inconsistent WITHIN one view: Daily loss limit reports -101.25 against -1000, Max trades per session reports 4 against 8, Max consecutive losses reports 5 against 3 -- three rules tell the operator where they stand and the sizing one, the one in breach, does not. F-9's remedy applies: derive the display FROM the same position data the enforcer uses. GetAccountSnapshots already iterates state.Positions.Values (to build PositionString), so the max single-instrument position quantity is in hand at snapshot-build time; it is simply not carried onto the snapshot or read by the evaluator.
tickets.spec: Carry the account's current MAX single-instrument position quantity (absolute) onto AccountStateSnapshot and report it as the 'Max contracts per account' rule's currentValue. Concretely: (1) add an int property MaxPositionQuantity to AccountStateSnapshot. (2) In GetAccountSnapshots, inside the existing `foreach (var pos in state.Positions.Values)` loop that builds PositionString, also track the maximum of Math.Abs(pos.Quantity) across the non-Flat positions and assign it to snapshot.MaxPositionQuantity (0 when flat). Do NOT add a second loop over positions -- fold it into the existing one. (3) In the 'Max contracts per account' evaluator in GuardRules.cs, replace the null first argument of R(...) with the account's MaxPositionQuantity: R(c.Account == null ? (double?)null : c.Account.MaxPositionQuantity, c.Config.Sizing.MaxContractsPerAccount, c.Account == null ? 0 : 1). The null-account branch must STILL report null (no account snapshot, no reading -- the same rule the equity evaluator uses via HasEquityReading). Change NOTHING about enforcement, the aggregate cap ('Max contracts aggregate' keeps its null -- its currentValue is a cross-account sum and is a separate slice), or the EvaluatedNotEnforcing state vocabulary. The evidenceCount argument (c.Account == null ? 0 : 1) is unchanged.

regions.note: Add the int MaxPositionQuantity property here beside AccountEquity/TradesToday. Add a property; reword nothing else -- neighbouring fields' comments are pinned by tests.

Populate MaxPositionQuantity inside the EXISTING `foreach (var pos in state.Positions.Values)` loop that builds PositionString -- track max Math.Abs(pos.Quantity) over non-Flat positions. Do not add a second loop and do not disturb PositionString.
Replace the R(null, ...) currentValue with c.Account.MaxPositionQuantity (null-account branch stays null). Do NOT touch the 'Max contracts aggregate' definition immediately below it.

expect_green: P2-132: the per-account contract cap reports the current max position, not null
P2-132: a flat account reports 0 for the per-account contract cap, not null
P2-132: the aggregate contract cap is untouched and still reports null
